facts.statement: The genus Mionetta was described by Livezey and Martin in 1988.
Mionetta lived from the Late Oligocene to the Middle Miocene in Western and Central Europe, including France, Germany, and the Czech Republic, and possibly Kazakhstan.
facts.quote: Mionetta is an extinct genus of duck from the Late Oligocene to Middle Miocene of Western and Central Europe (France, Germany and the Czech Republic), and possibly also Central Asia (Kazakhstan).

facts.statement: Many species originally assigned to Mionetta were previously classified within the genus Anas.
facts.quote: Many of the species were originally assigned to the genus Anas.

facts.statement: Mionetta is one of the earliest and best-known fossil ducks, with the type species M. blanchardi represented by thousands of specimens from the Early Miocene Saint-Gérand-le-Puy locality.
facts.quote: It is among the best and earliest known fossil members of the family Anatidae, with the type species M. blanchardi known from thousands of specimens collected from the Early Miocene (Aquitanian) Saint-Gérand-le-Puy locality.

facts.statement: The humerus bone features are diagnostic for identifying Mionetta.
facts.quote: Diagnostic characters include features of the humerus bone.

facts.statement: In its 1988 description, Mionetta was placed in the extinct subfamily Dendrocheninae alongside the genus Dendrochen.
facts.quote: In the original 1988 description of the genus it was placed as one of two genera in the extinct subfamily Dendrocheninae alongside Dendrochen.

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding Mionetta's classification: a 2008 study placed it in the subfamily Oxyurinae, while a 2022 study positioned it basally in Anatidae outside the split between Oxyurinae, Anatinae, and Anserinae.
facts.quote: A 2008 study considered it to be a basal member of the subfamily Oxyurinae, while a 2022 study placed in a basal position in Anatidae outside the split between Oxyurinae, Anatinae and Anserinae, though more closely related to these subfamilies than to Dendrocygna.

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists Oxyurinae as the parent group for Mionetta.
Mionetta belongs to the family Anatidae.
Mionetta lived between 33.9 and 15.98 million years ago, from the Rupelian to the Burdigalian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Rupelian to Burdigalian (33.9 to 15.98 million years ago)
